what_this_is: the ask-to-journey dictionary. A small model cannot hold ML methodology, so it does not have to: map_the_ask keyword-matches the person's sentence to one of these journeys and returns the ordered steps, each naming a REGISTERED tool and what to put in it. The model's job shrinks to relaying steps and filling blanks the person gives it.

journeys.what_unnecessary_if_means: The later step whose success makes this one moot. Somebody who arrives with graded rows cannot run carve_rows or drop_duplicates - there is no folder of documents to cut - and carve_eval_set succeeding proves rows existed and were good enough to split, which is what those two exist to produce. Marking them done would claim work nobody did; leaving them not started would demand work nobody needs. The route knows which is which, so the knowledge lives here rather than as a table in app/journey.py.
